preview: Interview experience for Graduate Technical Analyst at Deutsche Bank by Pranav Kute, detailing the online assessment, technical rounds, professional-fitment round, HR round, and useful preparation tips.
content: DEUTSCHE BANK INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE FOR 2024 FTE Pranav Kute Final Year B.Tech. Computer Engineering Student 2020-24 Deutsche Bank visited our campus in the first week of August to hire final year students for the role of Graduate Technical Analyst in Technology Data and Innovation (TDI) Business Division. Their criteria was: CPI : 7 and above, Branches : Computers, IT & EXTC. There were 5 rounds conducted overall. 1. Online Coding Test. 2. Technical Round-1. 3. Technical Round-2. 4. Professional-fitment Round. 5. HR Round. Online Assessment 4th August,2023. The proctored online assessment was conducted on the Hackerearth platform. Total time alloted was 90 minutes. There were 3 coding questions and each of them had an individual weightage of 20, 50 & 50 respectively. Power Limit - 20 points. Given 2 resources with powers A and B respectively. At each second, you have to select one resource out of 2 to run the software. The power of the resource at the time of selection should be greater than 1. Every second, the power of the selected resource gets reduced by 2 and the power of unselected resource gets charged by 1. The software stops when at least one resource has 0 power. You are given integers A and B. Print the maximum number of seconds your software can run if you select the resources optimally. Complete the function PowerLimit(). This function takes the following 2 parameters and returns the required answer: A: Represents the power of the first resource, B: Represents the power of the second resource. Auto Suggest - 50 points. N: Represents the number of words in the dictionary, words: Represents the dictionary, S: Represents the query word. Given a dictionary consisting of N words and a query word S. You need to auto-suggest the best word from the dictionary that is closest to S. Two words are first compared by their Levenshtein distance to the word S. If two words have the same Levenshtein distance, then the lexicographically smaller word is given priority. Levenshtein distance between two strings is defined as the minimum number of edits required to obtain one string from the other. An "edit" is defined by either an insertion of a character, a deletion of a character, or a replacement of a character. All the words and the query word S consist of lowercase alphabets only. Complete the function solve. This function takes the following 3 parameters and returns the required answer. Backlink Sorting - 50 points. WebPage: Represents an array of strings that contains the webpage titles, Backlinks: Represents an array of integers that contains the backlink count. Backlinks are links from other websites to a particular web resource, and they play a crucial role in the SEO of pages. You are given N web page titles and corresponding arrays that contain the number of backlinks for each web page. The objective is to rank the web pages in descending order based on the number of backlinks they have. Note: If two or more web pages have the same number of backlinks, maintain their original order. Complete the function Sorter. This function takes 2 parameters as arguments and returns the strings. I was able to solve all the 3 questions and pass all the testcases in them within the given time limits. The results of the online assessment were released after 3 days on 7th August, 2023. A total of 41 students were shortlisted for the offline interviews. Technical Round 1 (9th August, 2023 | 11:30 am - 12:45 pm): 1. Tell me about yourself. Since my resume and projects involved java a lot of questions on Java were asked to me. 2. What is JDK JRE JVM? 3. Explain encapsulation and abstraction with code. 4. What is autoboxing and unboxing? 5. What is the difference between final finally and finalise? 6. Expections and their types. 7. Explain each word of "public static void main(String [] args)". 8. What is static keyword? 9. Access modifiers and their types in java. 10. Given inorder and preorder traversal build a binary tree from it. 11. Intersection point of y-shaped linked list. 12. Isomorphic strings. 13. Write a query to find 4th highest salary give two variations. 14. Explain ACID properties. More 2-3 SQL queries were asked to me however I dont remember them. The interviewer then moved to React.js and javascript as it was mentioned in my resume. 15. Importance of package.json file. 16. Asynchronus functions. 17. Explain Redux. 18. Explain Cors. Why is it required? The round went pretty good I was able to answer all the questions. Out of the 41 students interviewed for Round 1, around 33 students were shortlisted for Round 2. Technical Round 2 (9th August, 2023 | 1:15 pm - 2:15 pm): 1. Tell me about yourself. 2. What is git and github? 3. Explain all the command required to push file to a github repository. 4. What is a merge conflict? When does it occur? How to resolve it? 5. What is git rebase command used for? 6. Write a code for merge sort. 7. What are Avl trees advantage over BST and explain their functioning. 8. Write a sql query for selecting only unique rows from a table without using distinct keyword. 9. Write a query for selecting the max salary in each department. More 2-3 SQL queries were asked to me however I dont recollect them. Again a fair bit of Java questions were asked. 10. What are servlets in java? 11. What is jsp? 12. What is jdbc? 13. Ellaborate the work done in internship. The round again went pretty good I was able to answer all the questions. Out of the 33 students interviewed for Round 2, around 31 students were shortlisted for Round 3. The interviewer then asked me about the sorting algorithms I was aware of. The interviewer then asked me if I had any questions. I asked her about her experience at Deutsche bank so far and what sets DB apart from the other banks. Professional-Fitment Round (9th August, 2023 | 3:15 pm - 3:50 pm): 1. Tell me about yourself. 2. Why DB? 3. Josephus Problem. 4. Discussion on projects and tech stack used. 5. Ellaborate on the work done in summer internship. 6. As my internship was in Bangalore.. he asked some questions like How was Bangalore?! 7. What is your Family Background? The round again went pretty good. Out of the 31 students interviewed for Round 3, around 26 students were shortlisted for Round 4. HR Round (9th August, 2023 | 5:45 pm - 6:20 pm): 1. Tell me about yourself. 2. Why DB? 3. Some brief discussion on projects. 4. What domain do you wish to explore? 5. What is your family Background? 6. What will I choose if I get a PPO at my summer internship company as well as DB offer? 7. Some (2-3) HR questions were asked.. however I don't remember them. The interviews concluded around 8:15 PM and we got the results within 15-20 minutes. All the 26 candidates who gave the HR round were selected and I was lucky to be one among them. Tips: Related to DSA: Data Structures & Algorithms : 450dsa (recommended) or striver's list. 1. Keep some hard copies of your resume handy. Since some companies take offline interviews, they do ask for hard copies. 2. Be very thorough with your CS fundamentals. Don’t neglect it and leave it for the end. 3. When you don’t understand a particular problem statement, do ask for clarifications on it. 4. Think out loud. This way the interviewer gets an idea about which direction you are headed and may help you start thinking in the right direction. This also keeps the interview interactive. 5. Make sure to go through all projects on your resume and be prepared for questions that can be asked about them like why did you use this technology/framework instead of that technology/framework, difference between two frameworks, etc. 6. It is alright to tell them that you don’t know a particular thing instead of bluffing about it and getting caught. They don’t expect you to know everything. They are more interested in seeing how you use the knowledge you have and apply your logic to tackle an unseen problem statement. Lastly, keep calm during your interviews and have confidence in yourself. All the best !! Related to Core CS(OS, DBMS, OOPS): https://whimsical.com/object-oriented-programming-cheatsheet-by-love-babbar-YbSgLatbWQ4R5paV7EgqFw, https://whimsical.com/operating-system-cheatsheet-by-love-babbar-S9tuWBCSQfzoBRF5EDNinQ, https://whimsical.com/dbms-roadmap-by-love-babbar-FmUi8ffVop33t3MmpVxPCo. For both CS/non-CS students - Gate Smashers OS and DBMS is more than sufficient for both academics and interviews. Don't just binge watch the lectures but make some notes on OneNote/Notion/Docs (not traditional notes but screenshots would do - screenshots helped me a lot during revision). For OOPS, use any resource available online in your language of choice (prefer C++, Java or Python) and cover the major concepts in it. Some Resources Related to Interviews.
